name: antenatal care overview
title: Antenatal care from first suspicion to term: what to assess, test and act on at each stage (confirm and date, first visit, second trimester, third trimester), then how the first-visit group and screen splits into Rh negative without an antibody (Rh immunoglobulin) and an antibody found (titre, middle cerebral artery Doppler, timing of delivery); panels on teratogens (timing, physical, infectious, maternal), drug risk categories and counselling, and who cares for her

root.title: Antenatal care: what do I assess, test and act on at THIS visit?
lines: after 20 weeks, ANY headache or sudden severe edema: exclude preeclampsia → HYPERTENSION chart
lifestyle, food, nausea and safe medicines: see the EARLY PREGNANCY COUNSELLING chart

groups.title: Visit by visit, in order
lines: each stage adds to the last

groups.title: The first-visit GROUP AND SCREEN decides
lines: is she Rh negative, and is there an ANTIBODY?

head: h
1 · Suspect, confirm, date
before the first visit
assess: • the first sign if cycles are regular
• irregular cycles or on the pill: spotting or lighter menses instead
test: 1 · Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), urine or serum
• serum < 5 negative · 5–25 very early or error · > 25 = pregnant
• most useful: irregular cycles, recurrent miscarriage, previous ectopic
2 · ultrasound: YOLK SAC needed, a gestational sac alone does not confirm
3 · where is it? → FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart
act: • Naegele: last normal menstrual period + 7 days − 3 months + 1 year
• in vitro fertilization: embryo TRANSFER DATE overrides every ultrasound
• else first-trimester crown-rump length; any scan < 23 wk beats the period
• once set, FIXED: a later different scan = growth, not a new date
• dating scan → ULTRASOUND THROUGH PREGNANCY chart

head: h
2 · First visit
first trimester, to 14 weeks
assess: • every medication + exposure → TERATOGEN + DRUG RISK panels
test: • 11–14 wk: genetic screen → PRENATAL GENETIC SCREENING chart
• hemoglobinopathy: Mediterranean, Southeast Asian, African, or low mean cell volume
• hepatitis C, herpes simplex: high risk only, NOT routine
act: • folic acid (600 mcg) + iron (27 mg): most often needed
• +350–450 kcal/day: healthy eating over weight gain

head: h
3 · Second trimester
14–28 weeks
assess: • normal: liner only, on wiping, brownish; after walking, exercise, sex
• ASSESS: frank red, fills a pad, pain, contractions, trauma
test: • low-lying placenta or previa: ANY spotting is investigated
act: • pertussis (Tdap) at 27–32 wk: her antibodies protect the baby
• influenza: any week, in flu season

head: h
4 · Third trimester → term
28 weeks on
assess: • LABOUR: rhythmic, regular, 20–60 s, minutes apart, stronger
• preeclampsia + HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets)
• after ANY trauma: seen in person
test: low: anemia work-up + iron on the PHYSIOLOGIC CHANGES chart

head: h
Rh NEGATIVE, no antibody
Rh immunoglobulin (RhIG) PREVENTS one
assess: • RhIG clears them before she makes an antibody
act: 2 · post-partum if the baby is Rh POSITIVE
Also after bleeding, a procedure or trauma

head: h
ANTIBODY found
it can cross the placenta: fetal anemia
assess: Why, and will the fetus carry it?
test: • peak systolic velocity tracks fetal hemoglobin
act: intrauterine transfusion of antigen-negative blood, serially

panels.title: Teratogen exposure: when and what
items: WHEN: weeks 1–2 usually NOT susceptible · weeks 3–8 (organogenesis) → MAJOR anomalies · fetal period → function + minor anomalies; central nervous system, eyes, genitalia sensitive to term
PHYSICAL: radiation, fetal dose NOT over 50 rads · hyperthermia, core ≥ 39°C (exercise does NOT reach it: keep exercising) → spontaneous abortion, neural tube, heart, abdominal wall defects

TORCH: cytomegalovirus = #1 infectious cause of birth defects, 40% on a first infection · herpes simplex in the last 3 months: 30–50% → CESAREAN · rubella: check titres · toxoplasmosis: NOT routinely screened
Maternal DIABETES: neural tube, central nervous system, spine, heart, limb defects → glycemic control + folic acid BEFORE conception

panels.title: Drug risk: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) category
items: A: controlled HUMAN studies, no risk · doxylamine-pyridoxine, folic acid, levothyroxine
B: no human studies, ANIMALS show no risk · amoxicillin, loratadine, ondansetron
C: NO studies in animals or humans = no data, NOT 'safe' · fluconazole, metoprolol, sertraline
D: HUMAN risk, benefit may outweigh it · paroxetine, diazepam, lisinopril, phenytoin, lithium
X: risk outweighs ANY benefit · methotrexate, simvastatin, warfarin
nausea: Diclectin (doxylamine-pyridoxine) is the ONLY approved antiemetic
Planning pregnancy: optimize the disease · fewest drugs, lowest dose · switch if possible · folic acid 1 mg on antiepileptics · ask FRAME (Fetal Risk After Maternal Exposure)

panels.title: Who looks after her
items: LOW risk: family physician (cares for the baby too, for years) or midwife (home, birth centre or hospital; mother + baby to 6 weeks; informed CHOICE, not informed consent)
obstetrician: consultant for the complicated case · every form of delivery incl. cesarean · NO infant care, no lactation training
CONSULT obstetrics: diabetes, essential hypertension, prior preeclampsia, high body mass index, lupus · abnormal fetal surveillance · planned cesarean
labour: dystocia, operative or cesarean birth, preeclampsia · post-partum: major hemorrhage, 3rd/4th-degree tear
